tagline: Up the Kennebec and over the north woods to Quebec.
intro: US 201 leaves Solon at the Robbins Hill overlook and follows the Kennebec north through Bingham, past Wyman Lake and the 155-foot Wyman Dam of 1930, to The Forks, where the Dead River comes in. There the road leaves the river. It climbs into the north woods over Johnson Mountain and around Coburn Mountain to the Attean Pond lookout, then drops into Jackman and runs on to the Quebec line, 78 miles from Solon.

The Abenaki traded along these rivers first, and in 1775 Benedict Arnold took his army up the Kennebec toward Quebec. The town at the top is named for Captain James Jackman, hired in the 1830s to build the road.
season: Foliage typically peaks from late September through early October.

moments.title: The Forks
moments.text: A plantation of 48 people where the Dead River meets the Kennebec, and the byway's place for whitewater rafting.

moments.title: Attean Pond Lookout
moments.text: The road tops out at this rest area, looking out over the Moose River valley, before it starts down into Jackman.

moments.title: Jackman
moments.text: A town of fewer than a thousand that drew more than 10,000 people for the 2024 eclipse, when Jackman was expected to have clear skies. Probably the largest crowd it has seen.
